rationale: Historic England 1079145 Details, cached via the British Listed Buildings OGL mirror (HE returns 403 to the downloader): 'Late C17, by Wren, incorporating work of early C16 and early C17'. Matches a manual read of the HE page.
Read America's National Churchill Museum history: 'In 1965 the removal process began', 7,000 stones shipped; foundation stone laid October 1966. Seed 1964 kept as reported alternative, not chosen.
Custodian history states work began 1672 and was essentially complete by 1677, cupola 1679. Verified as the body interval this source reports; seed 1670-74 remains a differing alternative.
Historic England 1080836 Details: 'Tower of All Hallows, Lombard Street by Wren, re-erected 1940 as tower of new Church'.
Historic England 1079973 Details: spire upper part 'Brought from demolished Church by Sir Christopher Wren in City of London', now at Round Hill SE26.
Article paragraph states the upper spire was replaced in 1829 and the removed portion sold to Robert Harrild. Verified as what this source reports; official listing gives no year.
Article states the ten bells were transferred to All Hallows Lombard Street when St Dionis was demolished; names the other church directly.
Read detailed official history: explicit resemblance to St James Garlickhythe and St Michael Paternoster Royal. Verify reported comparison, not inferred influence.
Official Abchurch history explicitly names Kempster and the three other church projects; retain wording about Walbrook collaboration with Strong.
Official architectural description states interior dome largely carried on walls; do not verify surrounding promotional or priority claims.
Official detailed history describes dome carried by columns and walls; verify described feature, not asserted artistic value or influence.
Read official listing's history and component description: body/spire destroyed in 1941, tower stages retained. Verify component destruction, not total site loss.
Official listing contains both 1966 and 1967. Verify the reporting window as stated, keeping uncertainty about milestones rather than claiming an exact completion year.
Read article and official entry; both report 1670-1679 construction. Retain Hooke/Wren office authorship caveat.
Read official detailed history by Kerry Downes: foundation stones 17 December 1672. Verify reported milestone, not completion interval.
Official history states ready for use when dinner was planned 27 May 1679. Retain this specific milestone without resolving all-fabric date dispute.
Read official detailed history reporting later steeple 1713-1717; separate from church body.
Read official wartime page: air raid in 1941 and church dome damage. Do not claim total destruction or unverified restoration year.
Published hours read on official Contact & Visit Us page; verified as published information on review date, not live availability.
Official visitor page explicitly states weekends/festivals and early private-event closures; retain contact/calendar advice.
Official homepage announces nine-month closure from about 12 October 2026. Record approximate date and unknown reopening; supersedes general history-page opening statement.
Read cafe's official page, linked from church site. Verify cafe hours only, not unrestricted church opening.
Official cafe page requires booking when working over 1.5 hours; do not apply condition to short tourist visits without evidence.
Read official Historic England Details passage; Wren attribution is explicit and corroborates article p[6]. No resolution of differing construction end years is implied.
Read official church Details and article post-fire history; Wren attribution agrees.
Read official church Details and article post-fire history; verify attribution only, not discrepant dates.

Official 1686-94 range agrees with article start and completion; preserve interruption caveat.
